samples.summary: New `readOnly` guard on `YorkieStore.undo`/`redo` has no test
samples.evidence: This delta adds `if (this.readOnly) return { success: false };` to both `undo()` (yorkie-store.ts:1285) and `redo()` (:1291), documented as the enforcement point that keeps a viewer-role share-link visitor from writing through a history replay ("nothing stands between a viewer-role visitor and this method — the store is the enforcement point"). The only suite over this code, `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store-undo.test.ts`, constructs every store as `new YorkieStore(doc, TabA)` (line 41) — the default `readOnly = false` — and never instantiates a read-only store; grep for `readOnly` in that file returns nothing. So the guard is never exercised: deleting either line leaves the whole suite green, and a regression that re-opens undo for viewers ships undetected. Constructing the case is one line (`new YorkieStore(doc, TabA, ..., true)`) in a file that already drives real undo/redo against a detached Yorkie doc.

samples.summary: The `onUndoJumpHandled` consume-once lifecycle — the point of this delta — is untested
samples.evidence: The delta adds `onUndoJumpHandled` so a consumed `undoJumpTarget` is cleared by the host, with the stated failure mode that a stale target is re-applied after any remount (datasource/lakehouse tab round trip, loader branch), re-selecting cells from an undo long past. Grepping `onUndoJumpHandled|undoJumpTarget|onUndoJump` across the repo returns only the three source files and two docs — no test file. No frontend test renders `SheetView`, `DocumentLayout` or `SharedDocumentLayout` (checked the full `packages/frontend/src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}` list), even though comparable view-level tests exist (e.g. `docs-view-readonly.test.tsx`, `shared-notes-layout.test.tsx`). So the fired-once-then-cleared behavior, and the remount-does-not-re-apply behavior it exists for, have no coverage; a regression that drops the callback or the `setUndoJumpTarget(null)` would be silent.

samples.summary: New focusUndoSelection tests assert only mock call routing against a hand-built context
samples.evidence: `createContext()` (line 40) stubs every collaborator (`selectStart`, `selectEnd`, `selectRow/RowRange`, `selectColumn/ColumnRange`, `worksheet.render`, `revealActiveCell`, `notifySelectionChange`) and the method is invoked via `focusUndoSelection.call(ctx, ...)` on a plain object rather than a real `Spreadsheet`. The assertions are purely "this mock was called with these args", so nothing verifies the resulting selection state, and a future dependency added to `focusUndoSelection` (e.g. a `_readOnly` or tab-id check reading a field the fake context lacks) would silently change behavior while these tests stay green. The branch coverage itself is real and reasonable — this is a limitation to note, not a blocker; the file follows the existing `spreadsheet-readonly-recalc.test.ts` precedent.

verdict.reason: The readOnly guard on YorkieStore.undo/redo is real (yorkie-store.ts:1285, 1291) and genuinely has no test. I searched beyond the reviewer's paths and found the read-only suite they missed — packages/frontend/tests/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store-read-only.test.ts — which does construct read-only stores (line 68, lines 190-194) and meaningfully covers presence seeding, updateSelection, ensureAxisOrder and comment writes; but I read it in full and it never invokes undo() or redo(). A grep for undo|redo across packages/frontend/tests/app/spreadsheet and packages/frontend/tests/helpers returns zero matches. The only undo suite (yorkie-store-undo.test.ts) builds every store writable (lines 41, 155), and its {success:false} assertion at lines 170-173 exercises the empty-history branch (lines 1286/1292), not the readOnly branch. The sheets-package ReadonlyStore.undo/redo (packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts:327-341) and the notes/docs read-only suites are different classes and cannot fail if lines 1285/1291 are deleted. There is no e2e directory. Deleting either guard line leaves the whole suite green, so a regression re-opening history replay for a viewer-role visitor ships undetected — a missing test over a new guard, squarely in the test-adequacy lane.

finding.summary: `Spreadsheet.focusUndoSelection` — the entire cross-tab undo landing path — has no test
finding.evidence: `focusUndoSelection` contains real branching (row → selectRow/selectRowRange, column → selectColumn/selectColumnRange, cell → selectStart/selectEnd only when the range is not a single cell, plus render/reveal/notify). Grepping the repo for `focusUndoSelection` returns only its definition (packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:689) and its single call site (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/sheet-view.tsx:1454) — no test file mentions it. The two new sheets test files cover `resolveUndoSelection` and `Sheet.applyUndoSelection`, but nothing exercises the view-level restore, which is the only code that makes a cross-tab undo visible to the user. A defect here (e.g. off-by-one in the `end.r > start.r` guard, or the cell branch leaving a stale multi-range) ships silently.

verdict.reason:
The finding claims `Spreadsheet.focusUndoSelection` has no test and that grepping for it returns only its definition and call site. That is false in this working tree. `packages/sheets/test/view/spreadsheet-undo-selection.test.ts` is a dedicated, branch-complete test for exactly this method, and it surfaced in the first grep for `focusUndoSelection` as well as in a glob of `packages/sheets/test/**/*.ts` — the two searches the reviewer reported as empty.

The test is not vacuous and not over-mocked: it extracts the real `Spreadsheet.prototype.focusUndoSelection` (test:34-38) and invokes it via `.call(ctx, ...)`, so the actual branching at spreadsheet.ts:689-707 executes. Only the collaborators the method delegates to (`sheet.select*`, `worksheet.render`, `worksheet.revealActiveCell`, `notifySelectionChange`) are stubbed, and those calls are the method's entire observable contract — there is no logic mocked away.

Coverage maps onto every branch the finding enumerates: row single (test:121-138) vs. row span (test:140-156); column single and spanning (test:158-186); cell single-cell with no `selectEnd` (test:63-84) vs. multi-cell `selectEnd` (test:86-102) and column-only difference (test:104-119); the `!selection.range` early return (test:188-198); and the `!this.sheet` early return (test:200-217). Both defects the finding specifically hypothesizes are caught: an off-by-one loosening `end.r > start.r` to `>=` fails the `expect(selectRowRange).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` assertion at test:136, and a stale multi-range from the cell branch fails `expect(selectEnd).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` at test:80. Render/reveal/notify are asserted with exact call counts (test:81-83).

The file is executed by the runner: packages/sheets/vite.config.ts declares no custom `test.include`, so vitest's default `**/*.test.ts` pattern picks it up, in the same directory as existing sibling tests such as spreadsheet-readonly-recalc.test.ts.
